title: OpenAI-compat: non-blocking ACK handshake and tolerant tool-schema validation
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: we observed two classes of production failures when using the OpenAI compatibility layer for function/tool calling: 1) streaming callers stalled when the hosted model emitted an early 'ack' or partial control token that the adapter treated as a terminal tool invocation; 2) strict schema validation rejected useful, partial tool payloads produced by some open models, causing noisy fallbacks and user-facing errors. This PR introduces a non-blocking ACK handshake pattern for framed tool/function messages plus a tolerant schema validation mode that accepts partial/approximate payloads and annotates provenance for downstream consumers. Changes include: a) protocol change: add an optional ack event type (openai_ack) that is treated as advisory in streaming mode and does not immediately finalize the invocation unless followed by a definitive 'invoke' envelope; b) emitter/backpressure: runtime now uses a lightweight debounce to coalesce adjacent control frames and emits a backpressure hint when an ack is received without a matching payload; c) schema validation: implement "tolerant" validation with configurable thresholds (missing_keys_threshold, type_coercion=true) and annotate accepted-but-incomplete payloads with _rw_provenance tags; d) compatibility: adapter layer maps both "tool" and "function" naming in user-facing events and preserves legacy fields for clients depending on exact OpenAI framing; e) safety: added guardrails so tolerant mode never accepts payloads that would escalate privileges or change routing metadata; f) observability: new metrics (openai_ack_count, ack_coalesce_ratio, partial_payload_accepts) and logs mark tolerant-decisions to support audits; g) docs and SDK updates: examples for Python/TS showing how to opt into tolerant mode and how to interpret provenance annotations. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked in Linear ENG-4721; - [x] unit + integration tests for ack-handshake; - [x] stress test for streaming stability with variable fragment sizes; - [x] docs updated; - [x] migration notes for customers. Impact: should reduce spurious fallbacks and streaming stalls observed in canary clusters while preserving deterministic invoke semantics when models emit explicit invoke envelopes. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag openai_ack_tolerant; enabled in canary subset for 72h, then 7-day extended canary, then global rollout pending telemetry.
commits_summary: 4 commits; initial protocol shim + tests; runtime debounce + metrics; schema tolerant validator + annotation; docs and SDK examples
review_comments: Ethan Cole: Can you clarify when an ack will be considered authoritative vs advisory? Suggest adding a short state diagram in the docs.
Rina Sato: Important to ensure tolerant validator cannot accept routing keys or authority fields. Please add a unit test that mutates routing metadata and assert rejection.
Omar Vasquez: CI flake observed on adapter_test; looks like timing assumption in debounce. Suggest using a deterministic clock in tests.
Author (Maya): Addressed: added state diagram to docs, added explicit routing-key rejection tests, switched debounce tests to fake clock.
release_notes: Introduce optional non-blocking OpenAI-style ACK event that improves streaming stability; add tolerant tool/function schema validation mode with provenance annotations; new runtime metrics and SDK examples. Gate: openai_ack_tolerant runtime feature flag.
notes_on_migration: Operators: enable openai_ack_tolerant in canary pools; monitor 'partial_payload_accepts' and 'ack_coalesce_ratio'; if you rely on strict validation, set tolerant mode off and opt into explicit invoke-only behavior. Customers using custom tooling that depends on exact OpenAI framing should test with SDK examples provided.
testing_summary: Added unit tests for tolerant validator (edge cases for missing keys/type coercion), adapter tests for ack vs invoke flows, integration test simulating high fragment jitter; ran 24h stress on canary cluster: observed 67% reduction in stalled streams and 12% lower fallback rates for the sampled workload.
risk_and_rollout: Low-medium. Protocol change is additive and gated. Tolerant validation increases surface for accepting malformed payloads but includes explicit routing rejection and safety heuristics. Rollout: canary 72h -> extended 7 days -> global. Quick disable via runtime flag.
